communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Vincent M. Battle
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- Personnel, assignment and performance records for Vincent Martin Battle (also known as Vincent M. Battle), a career Foreign Service officer who served from 1977 to approximately 2004, including assignment histories, Employee Evaluation Reports, promotion and tenure records, awards and commendations, and records of his retirement or separation, between January 1, 1977 and the date of search.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's 2001 nomination and appointment as U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon, including biographical sketches, nomination and clearance packages, any questionnaire or statement prepared for the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, his confirmation hearing testimony, swearing-in records, and records of his presentation of credentials, between January 1, 2001 and December 31, 2001.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's service as chargé d'affaires ad interim at U.S. Embassy Beirut in 1994 and as Ambassador to Lebanon from 2001 to 2004, including his arrival and farewell cables and any end-of-tour or end-of-mission reports, between January 1, 1994 and December 31, 2004.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's volunteer, When Actually Employed (WAE) or other service at U.S. Embassy Beirut after his retirement, including during the July–August 2006 evacuation of U.S. citizens from Lebanon, between August 17, 2004 and the date of search, including the following words/phrases: "Battle," "Ambassador Battle," "Vince Battle," "volunteer," "WAE," "evacuation."

Please search, at a minimum, the Bureau of Global Talent Management (formerly the Bureau of Human Resources), the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, U.S. Embassy Beirut, the Bureau of Consular Affairs, the Office of the Historian and the Executive Secretariat, as well as the Department's central cable and records systems.

Mr. Battle is deceased. Proof of death is attached (U.S. Embassy Beirut statement of October 5, 2026, and published obituary). Because Mr. Battle has died, his privacy interest is greatly diminished, and records relating to his official public service as a senior U.S. diplomat carry substantial public interest.

title: Sacramento Sheriffs Office Shoot Of Ingold Guttenbeil

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Sacramento Sheriffs Office Shoot Of Ingold Guttenbeil
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A. The October 4, 2026 shooting (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1)(A)(i))

This incident involved the discharge of firearms at a person by peace officers, so all records listed in § 832.7(b)(2) are subject to disclosure, including:

All investigative reports, including incident, supplemental, and use-of-force reports.
All photographic, audio, and video evidence, including body-worn camera, dash/in-car camera, surveillance or business video collected from the car wash or neighboring businesses, and any bystander video the Office obtained.
All 911 call audio, dispatch radio audio, and CAD records for the call that prompted the response.
Transcripts or recordings of interviews with deputies, witnesses, and the reporting party.
The autopsy report and any coroner's records in the Office's possession.
All materials compiled and presented to the District Attorney or any other body charged with determining whether to file charges, or whether the deputies' conduct complied with law and policy.
All documents setting forth findings or recommended findings, and any disciplinary records relating to the incident.
The names, badge numbers, and assignments of the three deputies who fired. Officer names are not confidential. (Commission on Peace Officer Standards & Training v. Superior Court (2007) 42 Cal.4th 278.)
Records identifying the firearm the Office reports recovering, its location when found, and any evidence-collection or chain-of-custody records documenting where it was found.

B. Critical incident video (Gov. Code § 7923.625)

Separately from Part A, I request all video and audio recordings of this critical incident. The Office has stated publicly that it intends to release body-worn camera footage. If release is delayed, please state the specific basis for the delay in writing, as the statute requires.

C. Related incidents involving Mr. Guttenbeil (Gov. Code §§ 7923.610, 7923.615)

The Office has publicly linked Mr. Guttenbeil to two prior incidents. I request the information the statute requires to be disclosed for:

The alleged shooting at the Marconi/Eastern intersection on the night of October 3, 2026: time, date, and location; time and date of report; factual circumstances; description of any injuries, property, or weapons involved; and CAD records.
The June 2026 arrest at the same intersection for suspected assault with a deadly weapon: arrestee information, factual circumstances of the arrest, charges, and the disposition.

D. Prior records of the involved deputies (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1))

For each of the three deputies who fired, all records of any other incident involving:
the discharge of a firearm at a person;
use of force resulting in death or great bodily injury;
a sustained finding of unreasonable or excessive force;
failure to intervene;
dishonesty;
unlawful arrest or search;
prejudice or discrimination.

E. Policies

The Office's use-of-force policy, de-escalation policy, body-worn camera policy, and critical-incident video release policy in effect on October 4, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

communications.subject: Louisiana Public Records Law Request: Incident Report Data
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Louisiana Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

For purposes of this request, "officer" means a sworn member of the police of any rank, and "data" means logs, tables, or datasets maintained in a machine-readable format (such as spreadsheets or database exports).
The timeframe for all portions of this request is all responsive records that exist in a machine-readable format from January 1, 2020 through the most recent date data is collected, and that can be produced as a spreadsheet or similar electronic file.
I request data sufficient to show any and all information maintained by the New Orleans Police Department regarding incident and offense reports recorded in NOPD's records management system. This should include all incidents recorded by NOPD regardless of whether the incident resulted in arrest, regardless of clearance status, and regardless of whether the underlying call was generated through 911, non-emergency line, officer-initiated activity, or walk-in/online reporting.
This request is specifically for the full underlying incident record set, including data fields that are not currently included in any publicly-released file on data.nola.gov (including the "Electronic Police Report" datasets) or any other public release. I am aware that subsets of NOPD incident data are published publicly. The publicly-released files omit fields that are necessary for the research purposes of this request, including but not limited to the originating CAD event identifier needed to link incidents to calls for service handled by OPCD, full offense-level detail in multi-offense incidents, victim and offender demographic detail, clearance status with date, and reporting officer assignment. I am requesting all fields below that exist in the underlying record system, regardless of whether they currently appear in any public release. A referral to a publicly-released subset is not responsive to this request.
Please provide the data in CSV, TXT, or XML format (machine-readable; not XLSX). For each incident, please include the following fields where they exist in the system:
Identifiers and CAD Linkage

Item Number (NOPD)
Originating CAD Event Number (the field needed to link this incident to the corresponding CAD record in OPCD calls-for-service data)
Case Number (if distinct from item number)
Linked Arrest Identifier(s), if any arrests resulted from the incident

Incident Timestamps

Date and Time of Incident (occurrence start)
Date and Time of Incident End (if range recorded)
Date and Time Reported to NOPD
Date and Time of Clearance (if cleared)

Incident Location

Address (block-level / hundred-block) or intersection
Latitude / Longitude

Zone or subdistrict

ZIP code

Offense Information (one record per offense)

Offense Sequence Number within the incident
Offense Code (NOPD signal code, NIBRS code if available, and Louisiana Revised Statutes / NOLA Municipal Code section)
Offense Description
Offense Class or Degree (felony, misdemeanor, municipal ordinance violation)
Attempted vs. Completed indicator
Weapon / Force Used
Bias Motivation / Hate Crime indicator
Domestic Violence indicator
Drug-Involved indicator

Victim Information (one record per victim, where applicable)

Victim Sequence Number
Victim Type
Age (or Year of Birth)
Sex
Race
Ethnicity (if stored separately from race)
Injury Type(s)
Relationship of Victim to Offender(s)

Offender / Suspect Information (one record per offender, where applicable)

Offender Sequence Number
Age (or Year of Birth)
Sex
Race
Ethnicity (if stored separately)
Whether the offender was identified or unknown at time of report

Clearance and Disposition

Disposition Code (NOPD uses dispositions including RTF for report to follow, NAT for necessary action taken, GOA for gone on arrival, UNF for unfounded, and others)
Clearance Status
Date of Clearance
Whether the incident is currently classified as Founded or Unfounded

Property Information (one record per property element, where applicable)

Property Sequence Number
Property Loss Type
Property Description
Property Value

Reporting Officer Information

Reporting Officer First Name
Reporting Officer Middle Name or Initial
Reporting Officer Last Name
Reporting Officer Badge Number or Item Number
Reporting Officer Rank or Title
Reporting Officer Employee ID (if tracked separately from badge number)
Reporting Officer Unit or Assignment at the time of report (district, platoon, or specialized unit)

Optional, if maintained in the system

Reporting Officer Race or Ethnicity
Reporting Officer Gender

If any of the above fields are stored under different names, codes, or tables, I request the functional equivalent fields. If incident data is stored across multiple linked tables, I would prefer to receive each table with its native keys preserved so the relationships can be reconstructed, including the link from the incident record to the originating CAD event.
Please also provide a codebook or data dictionary so that the data provided can be appropriately understood, including the NOPD signal code list, the disposition code list, and any internal clearance code definitions used in the export. If a Zoom call or meeting is preferred to a codebook, that is fine.
If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law. To the extent any individual field above is exempt under La. R.S. 44:3 or any other exception, please redact only that field and produce the remainder.
Please confirm receipt of this request within three business days as required by La. R.S. 44:32 / 44:33, and provide a tracking number. I am happy to discuss scoping, format, or staged production by year if that would expedite response.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Please include the accounts of Political Officer J. Claiborne Gayden (GaydenJC@state.gov) and Political Specialist Issa Boursheh (BourshehIX@state.gov).
•	Records concerning any outreach initiative, “listening tour,” or series of consultations by U.S. Embassy Jerusalem with Israeli officials, think tanks, and non-governmental organizations regarding the building of formal networks of countries in Africa and Latin America in support of Israel in international organizations, from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including terms of reference, target lists, contact logs, briefing materials, and readouts.

Hallinan (HallinanMB@state.gov), Dana M. Helfenbein (HelfenbeinDM@state.gov), and Catherine Batruni (BatruniC@state.gov). This includes any record discussing the application of the Chatham House Rule or the non-recording of these sessions.

INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SEARCH:
1.	Instructions Regarding “Leads”: As required by the relevant case law, the Department should follow any leads it discovers during the conduct of its searches and perform additional searches when said leads indicate that records may be located in another system. Failure to follow clear leads is a violation of FOIA.
2.	Request for Public Records: Please search for any records even if they are already publicly available.
3.	Request for Duplicate Pages: I request disclosure of any and all supposedly “duplicate” pages. communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Texas Public Information Act Request:ALL JustFOIA Cases - Smith County Sheriff
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting a copy of ALL Open Records Requests, "Texas Public Information Act Requests" also referred to as JustFOIA cases, received by the Smith County Sheriff's Office from September 1st, 2025 to September 1st, 2026. These are records in the JustFOIA records system, associated attachments, communications, etc. These requests in Sheriff's Office JustFOIA and other related records systems follow the typical naming or numbering system: "SO-0000-2026" or similar iterations. I am requesting all of those records, which have records numbers attached to them in the format just described, that are within the data range.

Include: All accepted, final and completed requests, all requests in this time frame that have not be resolved or concluded, and all requests that were completed but yielded no documents or material--including all denials as well.

Also include: all attachments, documentation, files and electronic communication (the communication of both parties about each request, the Sheriff's Office, and the requester in the JustFOIA system) included or relating to each request. And include the responsive material or documents for the requests-- including but not limited to: pdf files, xls files, jpeg images, doc and docx files, .eml and .msg files, electronic communications records,  etc.

Pull all records and results from JustFOIA system, or associated records management systems, using the already articulated date filter, Sept. 1 2025-Sept. 1 2026.

Please refer to Texas Public Information Act TGC 552 before issuing a denial that lacks a legitimate or statutory basis. 

The following qualifiers apply:

This records request is not one that requires new production of material or research of material. "A request for public information that requires a governmental body to program or manipulate existing data is not considered a request for the creation of new information." see:Fish v. Dallas Indep. Sch. Dist., 31 S.W.3d 678, 681-82 (Tex. App.—Eastland 2000, pet. denied); see Gov’t Code § 552.231; Attorney General Opinion H-90 (1973); Open Records Decision Nos. 452 at 2-3 (1986), 87 (1975). The claim that having to "research" material makes a request invalid, which is really querying computer systems for responsive materials, on face is nonsensical. Using that logic, any records retrieval would constitute "research", or subsequent exportation or dissemination of material would constitute creation of "new" material, both inferences are equally ridiculous. Retrieving responsive records does not constitute research, it is document production done in accordance with 552.

"A governmental body is not required to compile or extract information if the information can be made available by giving the requestor access to the records themselves", see Texas Atty General Open Records Handbook 2026, citing: Open Records Decision No. 243 (1980); Open Records Decision Nos. 512 (1988), 465 (1987), 144 (1976). Accordingly I am asking for original JustFOIA records. I am not asking for compiling, research, extracting, derivatives of preexisting information, etc. You only are obligated to compile information if you fail to provide the original source records.

This is a request for information already in existence, citing Gov’t Code §§ 552.002, .021, .227, .351.

 Additionally, 552.228(b) is applicable: "If public information exists in an electronic or magnetic medium, the requestor may request a copy in an electronic medium...". 552.228(a) is applicable as well: "  It shall be a policy of a governmental body to provide a suitable copy of public information within a reasonable time after the date on which the copy is requested."

Texas Public Info. Act includes no provision to exclude already existing or completed information requests themselves. See 552, broadly. Further, 552 applies to material in existence at time of the request.

If seeking to withhold information see 552.301(a, b). Broadly (a) & (b) stipulate that if a govt. body wishes to withhold, it must seek AG decision within ten business days of receipt of the request and state the disclosure exemptions it seeks, and the basis. Must be done to avoid noncompliance consequences per the statute. If Office fails to do this in timely manner, along with notification, requested info will be presumed open to public in accordance with the law.

In the event that you honor request SO-4764-2026 , I reserve the right to withdraw this request. 

Your office has certain obligations under TGC552, they entail reporting requirements and certain communications on your part. Also, binding timelines.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Piney Woods ALPR

TO: npsfoia@nps.gov; doee.foia@dc.gov; victoria.fleming@dcwater.com

CC: oig.hotline@epa.gov; oig_hotline@doioig.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; david.gadis@dcwater.com; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; callen@dccouncil.gov; serena_bellew@nps.gov; dondrae.maiden@sol.doi.gov; Square5815Oversight@gmail.com

DATE: Monday, October 5, 2026

SUBJECT: EXPEDITED MULTI-AGENCY FOIA REQUEST: Transcripts, Calendar Invites, and Metadata Logs for the October 1, 2026 Virtual Meeting Regarding Square 5815

Pursuant to the federal Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I hereby request expedited production of the following public records:

NARRATIVE CONTEXT & PRIOR KNOWLEDGE:
On Sunday, October 4, 2026, NPS Superintendent Serena Bellew confirmed in writing that a multi-agency virtual meeting was held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, between the National Park Service (NPS), the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE), and DC Water. Superintendent Bellew stated: "NPS, DC Water and DOEE had a virtual meeting last Thursday to coordinate next steps for addressing the elevated/exposed manhole cover/pipe on the site... DC Water explained that the pipe appears to be collapsed and blocked which is contributing to the water pooling."

Because this meeting involves federal and municipal agencies coordinating a response to an active infrastructure collapse, an unpermitted MS4 discharge, and biological contamination on​ a federal parkland​ swamp, I request the following records:

1. VIRTUAL MEETING PLATFORM RECORDS (Teams/Zoom/WebEx):
All digital records generated by the virtual meeting platform used to host the October 1, 2026 meeting. This specifically includes:
   - The auto-generated meeting transcript.
   - The audio/video recording of the meeting (if captured).
   - All in-meeting chat logs or instant messages sent between participants.
   - The complete digital attendee log showing the names, email addresses, and exact login/logout timestamps for every federal and municipal employee who joined the call.

2. CALENDAR METADATA & INVITATIONS:
The complete Microsoft Outlook, Google Workspace, or internal calendar invitation file (.ics or native format) for the October 1, 2026 meeting. This must include:
   - The original meeting description and agenda.
   - The complete list of invited attendees.
   - The RSVP metadata (Accepted/Declined/Tentative) for all invited federal and municipal personnel.

3. INTERNAL COORDINATION EMAILS:
All emails sent between NPS, DOEE, and DC Water personnel between September 28, 2026, and October 2, 2026, that contain the virtual meeting link, agenda, or subsequent follow-up action items resulting from the October 1 meeting.

4. HANDWRITTEN & DIGITAL NOTES:
All handwritten notes, digital notepad files, internal memos, or summaries created by Superintendent Bellew, Director Jackson, CEO Gadis, or their respective staff members during or immediately following the October 1 meeting, specifically concerning DC Water's admission of the "collapsed and blocked" pipe.

NATIVE FORMAT & METADATA PRESERVATION DEMAND:
Produce all electronic records in their native digital formats with all rich metadata intact. Do not "flatten" calendar invites or platform logs to PDF if such conversion destroys the underlying digital forensic metadata.

REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED PROCESSING:
Expedited processing is requested because there is an urgency to inform the public concerning actual government activity involving an active structural landslide and an uncontained public health biohazard adjacent to a designated public school pedestrian route.

REQUEST FOR FEE WAIVER:

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I request the records described below, created or received from July 1, 2017, through March 31, 2019.

Definition. In this request, "the Event" means a conference, symposium, or exhibition referred to as "SOFNEX" (including the variants "SOF NEX," "SOF-NEX," and "SOFNEX 2018"), focused on special operations forces and emerging technology, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, robotics and unmanned systems, big data, and intelligence analytics. Its organizers sought speakers and attendees from U.S. government agencies in 2017 and 2018. If the agency knows the Event under another name, please treat that name as an additional search term and tell me what it is.

Search terms. At a minimum, please search for: "SOFNEX"; "SOF NEX"; "SOF-NEX"; and the name of any organizer, venue, or alternate event title identified in the course of the search.

Records requested
1.	Foreign Visits System (FVS) and FVS Confirmation Module records, including visit requests, approvals, denials, and confirmations, for visits by Israel Defense Forces or Israeli Ministry of Defense personnel to Headquarters, U.S. Special Operations Command (MacDill AFB, Florida), or to events hosted or supported by USSOCOM, between January 1, 2018, and March 31, 2019. Names may be redacted if necessary; I ask that dates, sponsoring organizations, visitor units or offices, and stated purposes of visits be released.
2.	Any records in the FVS concerning visits connected to the Event (as defined above), regardless of the visitors' nationality. Names may be redacted if necessary.
Offices to search. The office within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy responsible for the Foreign Visits System and international security programs; the Defense Technology Security Administration; and any other OSD component that administers or maintains FVS records.

Instructions regarding search
•	Please follow any leads uncovered during the search, including referrals to other offices, record systems, or components, and conduct additional searches where those leads indicate responsive records may exist.
•	Please include records even if they are publicly available, and include all attachments to responsive emails.
•	"Records" includes emails and attachments, calendar entries and meeting invitations, memoranda, briefing papers, slide decks, letters, text and instant messages on government systems, approval forms, and handwritten notes. Please include drafts.
•	If any responsive records have been destroyed, please identify them and provide records relating to their destruction.
•	Please interpret the scope of this request broadly, short of an interpretation that would fail to reasonably describe the records sought.

Exemptions and segregability
Under the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), the Department of Defense may withhold information only if it reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption, or if disclosure is prohibited by law. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of any record, identify the exemption claimed for each redaction, and release pages even if all that remains after redaction is letterhead, dates, or administrative markings. Please black out, rather than remove, redacted material. Where names of third parties are withheld under Exemption 6, I ask that titles, offices, and organizational affiliations be released.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
